_healthy_comment: The healthy window is a SUBSET of the same payloads rather than a second file: healthy here means nothing reached the threshold and no verdict fell outside the grammar, which is a property of the window and not of a document. #9003 alone has one friction bullet, two in-grammar verdicts (a merge and a blocked verdict in the full wave shape -- SHA plus taught class -- #1240's keying) and no unlabelled bullet -- every key below the threshold of three and nothing off-grammar -- so every stats finding must be absent.
_comment: Shaped exactly as fetchWindow builds it: pr -> {body, comments:[{body}]}. Held as a fixture rather than fetched so the stats histogram is pinned without a network, a token, or a repository that happens to have the right history. Three `Fix review: blocked` verdicts and three `CLAUDE.md#budgets` friction entries put one key of each kind at the threshold; one verdict is deliberately outside the grammar in web-fix-wave.js so the drift report is pinned too. The friction entries are written in the template's grammar, `<rule_id>: <class>: <evidence>`, in the three spellings a body uses -- backticked id and class, bare, and unmarked by a list bullet -- so the histogram keys on the rule id the grammar names and not on whichever backticked span comes first; #9002's second bullet parses under no grammar and is the unlabelled bucket's one witness.
